notes.summary: Exact unchanged P16.4 scope and six caller-grant application register. O supplies the operator, while general equation existence and uniqueness are still required; no additional grant is inferred from working observation228.
notes.detailedSummary: Retains smooth geometrically integral projective varieties of arbitrary dimension, actual ample rational L, complete characteristic-zero real-valued fields with residue characteristic zero, raw intersection mass, arbitrary Radon support and every-point metrics. Indexes the complete O/D/N/T/Q/C bodies with their clarifications and distinguishes each granted conclusion from missing equation inputs. This is a scope and dependency register, not a new equation theorem.
notes.text:
Status and exact unchanged domain

This manuscript does **not** close original P16.4. Its new unconditional mathematical result is the finite graph interpolation theorem below, with a complete proof. It also proves a conditional actual curve equation, including loops, arbitrary Radon support, all-point uniqueness, the raw constants, and finite-orbit descent. The geometric antecedents of that conditional theorem have not all been verified under the requested recursive source rule. In particular, this submission does not assert an unconditional all-genus equation. The original arbitrary-dimensional equation remains open in this submission. Compilation, source retrieval, and finite arithmetic checks are not mathematical certification.

The unchanged original domain is a smooth geometrically integral projective variety $X$ of arbitrary dimension over a complete characteristic-zero real-valued non-Archimedean field $K$ with residue characteristic zero, and an actual ample rational line bundle $L$. Trivial, nontrivial, discrete, nondiscrete, and non-algebraically-closed fields are included. Write $T=X^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $V=(L^n)>0$. Targets have raw mass $V$. All metrics are actual all-point decreasing Fubini--Study net endpoints on the actual bundle, including literal pole values. P16.3, P16.5, and P16.7 are separate axes.

For a continuous psh reference $\psi$, scalars mean absolute metrics $\psi+u$. The continuous energy and its extension are
$$
 E_\psi(u)=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{j=0}^n\int_Tu\,\operatorname{MA}(u^{[j]},0^{[n-j]}),\qquad
 E_\psi(u)=\inf_{v\geq u,\ v\text{ continuous psh}}E_\psi(v).
$$
The first formula initially applies to continuous potentials; the second defines extended energy on actual singular endpoints. The class $\mathcal E^1$ consists of endpoints of finite extended energy. The target dual is
$$
 J_\psi(\mu)=\sup_{v\text{ continuous psh}}\left(E_\psi(v)-\int_Tv\,d\mu\right),\qquad \mu(T)=V.
$$
Constants cancel, since $E(u+c)=E(u)+Vc$. An actual reference change adds a finite constant to this dual. No measure is defined by naming an inverse target.

The six complete caller prerequisites

Only the complete supplied bodies O217, D214, N220, T171, Q222, and C218, including every supplied harmless clarification, are mathematical grants. Their historical draft headings do not override the caller's present accepted status. These labels are not registered supporting note IDs. This submission's emitted note n1 indexes their permitted use; subsequent supporting IDs refer only to emitted notes.

O gives the genuine actual mixed $\mathcal E^1$ operator over the entire original field and geometric domain, raw mass $V$, integrability of every actual $\mathcal E^1$ test against every mixed output, arbitrary directed weighted decreasing continuity, extended decreasing-energy continuity including $-\infty$, reference covariance, affine curvature calculus on admissible convex combinations, the segment polynomial and derivative, and complete-field pushforward. We use extended energy before asserting endpoint membership. Zero coefficients at poles are omitted. The supplied normalization correction handles nonpositive endpoints by shifting the reference and then letting the shift tend to zero; it is not a constrained regularization assumption.

D gives the jointly continuous completed-closure Galois action, the all-point quotient, actual invariant psh descent, extended energy equality, the unique invariant Radon lift, continuous-dual equality, and the continuous field laws. Its equation implication requires actual upstairs existence and uniqueness; it is not an existence theorem. Raw mass is preserved, without any field-degree factor.

N gives all-$\mathcal E^1$ integrability if and only if finite continuous dual **only after** a continuous actual reference with $\operatorname{MA}(0)=V\delta_\xi$ and $\sup u=u(\xi)$ for every FS scalar has been established. It cannot be applied to an unverified abstract graph reference. It gives coercivity, not attainment.

T gives the entire actual ample equation and every-solution all-point uniqueness over every trivially valued characteristic-zero field. Q gives the split projective-line equation, its actual disk atom metrics, its local disk classification, and every-solution all-point uniqueness. Q supplies no arbitrary-genus skeleton or model geometry. C gives strict Borel locality, open locality, and mixed and pure comparison for the genuine operator in O's domain. Comparison alone is not equation existence or every-solution uniqueness.

The complete supplied bodies are preserved as `sources/grant-O.tex`, `grant-D.tex`, `grant-N.tex`, `grant-T.tex`, `grant-Q.tex`, and `grant-C.tex`. The unchanged `input.json` preserves the complete caller input and clarifications. No historical review output or another campaign was read.

notes.summary: Independent finite-graph positive-curvature interpolation proof over any nonzero divisible real value subgroup, including irrational cycles, signed starting curvature and loops. Dirichlet kernels and maximum-support calculus are proved; this does not recognize an actual metric.
notes.detailedSummary: Solves the anchored finite Poisson system, makes the target strictly positive, approximates shared values in the value group and inserts one upward rational-slope bend per edge at a value-group location. Positive margins survive at old vertices, inserted curvature is positive, raw mass is preserved and both potentials and measures converge. Reconstructs symmetric nonnegative finite-core kernels, branch-extension monotonicity and the diffuse finite-graph maximum-support lemma. Exact checks cover 140 interpolation and 210 raw-mass cases only; analytic actuality is explicitly excluded.
notes.text:
Positive interpolation on graphs with irrational cycles

**Theorem 1 (finite graph statement).** Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonzero divisible additive subgroup. Let $G$ be a finite connected compact metric graph, with all edge lengths in $\Lambda$, and with positive fixed weights $w_e$. Let $\theta$ be a signed vertex measure of total mass $V>0$, and let $\mu$ be a nonnegative vertex measure of the same mass. Fix a vertex $z$. There is a unique continuous function $F$, affine on each edge, satisfying
$$
 F(z)=0,\qquad \theta+\Delta F=\mu,
$$
where $\Delta$ is the sum of weighted outgoing slopes. There are finite subdivisions and functions $G_i$ with rational slopes, vertex values in $\Lambda$, and one common denominator at each stage, such that
$$
 G_i\longrightarrow F\text{ uniformly},\qquad
 \theta+\Delta G_i\geq0,\qquad
 \theta+\Delta G_i\longrightarrow\mu\text{ weakly}.
$$
Every original vertex and every inserted bend has strictly positive curvature at each stage. This is a graph theorem, not a psh recognition theorem.

At an oriented interior bend with left slope $q_1$ and right slope $q_2$, the curvature atom is $w_e(q_2-q_1)$. At the initial endpoint the contribution is $w_eq_1$; at the terminal endpoint it is $-w_eq_2$. Thus an upward bend is positive and decreases the total curvature retained at the two old endpoints. All three contributions have sum zero. This is the positive outgoing-slope convention. KRZB's graph divisor uses its negative.

Subdivide a self-loop once at length $\ell/2\in\Lambda$, extending $\theta$ and $\mu$ by zero at the new vertex. This allows a proof with distinct endpoints for every edge; loops are not deleted. A one-vertex graph with no edges has $\theta=\mu=V\delta_z$, and $F=G_i=0$ suffices.

For an edge-affine function $H$, direct cancellation of edge contributions gives
$$
 -\sum_vH(v)\Delta H(v)=\sum_{e=ab}\frac{w_e}{\ell_e}\bigl(H(b)-H(a)\bigr)^2.
$$
Polarization proves symmetry of the vertex matrix. Connectivity makes its kernel exactly the constants. Its image is therefore precisely the zero-sum vectors. Anchoring at $z$ gives the claimed unique solution by finite-dimensional linear algebra. The same argument works with arbitrary positive real edge weights and signed $\theta$; no positivity of the starting model is used in this graph step.

Let there be $k$ original vertices after loop subdivision, and set $\rho=(V/k)\sum_v\delta_v$. For $0<\epsilon<1$ put
$$
 \mu_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)\mu+\epsilon\rho.
$$
Every original vertex has a positive curvature margin. The anchored solution $F_\epsilon$ to $\theta+\Delta F_\epsilon=\mu_\epsilon$ depends linearly on its right-hand side. Consequently $F_\epsilon\to F$ uniformly, with convergence of every original edge slope.

The subgroup $\Lambda$ is dense: if $a\ne0$ belongs to it, then $\mathbb Qa\subset\Lambda$ is dense. Approximate the finitely many shared vertex values $F_\epsilon(v)$ by $g_v\in\Lambda$, with $g_z=0$ and error at most $h$. For the oriented edge $a\to b$ put $d=g_b-g_a$ and $c=d/\ell$. The chord slope differs from the slope of $F_\epsilon$ by at most $2h/\ell$.

Choose rational numbers $q_1<c<q_2$, both within $\eta/2$ of $c$, and arrange $2h/\min_e\ell_e<\eta/2$. Strict bracketing is possible even when $c$ is rational. Set
$$
 t=\frac{d-q_2\ell}{q_1-q_2}.
$$
Because $q_1<c<q_2$, one has $0<t<\ell$. Because $\Lambda$ is a rational vector space, $t\in\Lambda$. Use slope $q_1$ from $a$ to $t$ and slope $q_2$ afterwards. The terminal value is exactly $g_b$, and the inserted vertex value $g_a+q_1t$ belongs to $\Lambda$. The same $g_v$ is used on every incident edge; compatibility around every cycle is exact. No claim that rational slopes on fixed irrational edges are dense is needed.

Every outgoing slope at an original vertex differs from the corresponding slope of $F_\epsilon$ by less than $\eta$. Choose
$$
 \eta\sum_{e\ni v}w_e<\frac12\mu_\epsilon(v)
$$
at every original vertex. Its new curvature is then at least half its positive margin. The single inserted point of each edge has mass $w_e(q_2-q_1)>0$. Total mass remains $V$, since $\Delta$ has total mass zero. The edgewise uniform error against $F_\epsilon$ is at most $h+\eta\ell_e$. The total inserted mass is less than $\eta\sum_ew_e$, and the old vertex masses converge to those of $\mu$ as first the approximation errors and then $\epsilon$ tend to zero. A diagonal sequence of these finite choices proves all the stated convergences. One common integer clears all rational slopes; multiplication by that integer preserves membership of every vertex value in $\Lambda$. Thus the approximants are integral $\Lambda$-affine after clearing denominators.

There is a genuine obstruction to the simpler fixed-edge strategy. On the two-edge cycle with lengths $1$ and $\sqrt2$, an edge-affine function with shared difference $d$ and rational slopes on both edges must have $d\in\mathbb Q\cap\sqrt2\mathbb Q=\{0\}$. Such functions are constant. Refining edges with movable positive bends removes this obstruction.

For the exact prototype $\theta=(1,1)$, $\mu=(2,0)$, $\epsilon=1/10$, the anchored difference is $d=(9/10)(2-\sqrt2)$. Slopes $(52/100,53/100)$ on the length-one edge and $(37/100,38/100)$ on the length-$\sqrt2$ edge give bend positions $-127+90\sqrt2$ and $-180+128\sqrt2$, respectively. The old masses are $189/100$ and $9/100$, and each new bend has mass $1/100$. Their sum is exactly $2$. These statements are proved by the formulas above and independently checked by exact arithmetic.

Finite-core Dirichlet kernels, including loops

In this section weights are one, as on a split skeleton over a complete algebraically closed field. Let $G$ be any finite connected compact metric graph and $z\in G$. Subdivide at points being used. Define $j_z(x,y)$ by
$$
 \Delta_xj_z(x,y)=\delta_z-\delta_y,\qquad j_z(z,y)=0.
$$
The preceding matrix proof gives existence and uniqueness, also on graphs with cycles. Define
$$
 D_G(f,h)=\sum_e\int_e f'h'\,dt=-\int_Gf\,\Delta h.
$$
The integration formula follows on each affine segment and by telescoping at vertices. It gives
$$
 D_G(j_z(\cdot,x),j_z(\cdot,y))=j_z(x,y)=j_z(y,x).
$$
The minimum principle gives $j_z\geq0$: a negative minimum is not at $z$, is incompatible with the negative sink mass at $y$, and otherwise propagates through zero outgoing slopes until it reaches $z$ or $y$. The maximum is at $y$ (or the kernel is zero when $y=z$).

Each edge slope of $j_z(\cdot,y)$ has absolute value at most one. For a regular level between zero and its maximum, sum $\Delta j_z$ over the vertices below that level and the corresponding partial edge segments. The crossing slopes are nonnegative, their sum is one, and each is at most one. Every nonconstant edge meets such a level. Symmetry therefore yields
$$
 |j_z(x,y)-j_z(x,y')|\leq d_G(y,y').
$$
This also proves joint continuity on $G^2$. The one-point/no-edge kernel is zero.

Suppose $G'$ is obtained by subdividing $G$ and attaching finite trees, each at a single point of $G$. Let $r:G'\to G$ collapse these trees. On an attached rooted tree write $\lambda(x,y)$ for the length of the common initial part of the two paths from its attachment point; put it equal to zero unless both points are in that same tree. Direct outgoing-slope cancellation, including the attachment vertex, gives
$$
 j^{G'}_z(x,y)=j^G_z(rx,ry)+\lambda(x,y).
$$
Both sides have the same source, sink, and anchor; uniqueness proves the formula. Adding several trees, or attaching them in stages, gives the same identity. Consequently the old kernel is unchanged when one point is in $G$, and the retracted kernels increase pointwise as branches are added. This is not an assumption that a graph with loops is a tree. The loops stay in $G$. Weighted branches would use resistance lengths $\ell/w$, not ordinary lengths; only unweighted upstairs branches are used below.

We also need a finite-graph maximum-support lemma. Let $h$ be a kernel potential with $\Delta h=\alpha-\sigma$, where $\alpha,\sigma$ are positive Radon measures of the same mass and $\sigma$ is supported on a nonempty finite set $S$. Then $\max_Gh=\max_Sh$. Indeed $h$ is Lipschitz with edge derivatives of bounded variation, by the kernel estimate. Put $M=\max_Sh$ and $b=(h-M)^+$. Edgewise Stieltjes integration by parts and vertex cancellation give
$$
 \sum_e\int_e|b'|^2=-\int_G b\,\Delta h
       =-\int_Gb\,d\alpha\leq0.
$$
Here $b=0$ on $S$, and $b'=\mathbf1_{\{h>M\}}h'$ almost everywhere. Thus $b$ is constant on the connected graph and vanishes on $S$. The claim follows. The integration formula can alternatively be obtained first with polygonal test functions, then by edgewise uniform and Sobolev approximation to $b$; the finite measure $\Delta h$ passes through uniform convergence. This is elementary one-dimensional graph integration, not a CLD smoothness assertion about a Thuillier lisse function.

Observation, not mathematical certification: graph_checks.py reported "all exact assertions passed". It exhaustively generated 140 interpolation cases and 210 raw-mass cases in its specified grids; kernel symmetry, branch-extension, the singleton case and a subdivided self-loop passed. The largest slope-grid denominator used was 512. The prototype original masses were 189/100 and 9/100, the two bends had mass 1/100 each, and their positions were -127+90 sqrt(2) and -180+128 sqrt(2). Arithmetic is exact in Q(sqrt(2)); it tests no analytic or formal model. The program and output are graph_checks.py, graph-checks-output.json, graph-checks.stdout.txt and graph-checks.stderr.txt. Rerun: python3 graph_checks.py.

notes.summary: Conditional actual all-genus curve equation with arbitrary Radon support, raw V^2/2 energy constants, every-solution terminal-value uniqueness and finite-orbit descent. Essential R1--R5 geometric realization hypotheses remain unverified, so no unconditional curve sector is claimed.
notes.detailedSummary: Assuming actual projective model realization, directed semistable retractions, local formal frames and terminal geometry, constructs continuous genuine atoms by n2 and actual nef/FS recognition. Uniform convex atom averages solve diffuse retracted targets; an anchored decreasing net has energy bounded by the genuine continuous dual before O gives E1 membership and the equation. Weighted curve symmetry determines finite-point values, local analytic section norms and upper semicontinuity recover all terminals, and concavity gives variational attainment. A finite continuous Galois-orbit atom average plus a proved graph maximum-support argument verifies N downstairs; D transfers only after actual upstairs existence and uniqueness. No higher-dimensional closure is asserted.
notes.text:
This is a mathematical implication relative to the complete caller prerequisites indexed in n1 and the independent graph results proved in n2. All additional geometric antecedents below remain explicit; they are not source-verified conclusions of this submission. The original field, bundle, mass and all-point requirements are retained.

Explicit conditional geometric antecedents

The following requirements are **additional hypotheses**, not conclusions about every original curve. They isolate the remaining bridge precisely.

(R1) Over a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field $C$, $X$ is a smooth connected projective curve with its actual ample rational $L$, $V=\deg L$. There is a finite semistable core $\Sigma_0$, with type-II vertices and edge lengths in $\Lambda=-\log|C^*|$, and an actual projective rational model of $L$ with metric $\psi_0$. Its component-degree measure $\theta$ is supported on that core and has raw mass $V$.

(R2) The finite skeleta containing $\Sigma_0$ form a directed family of continuous retractions $r_G:T\to G$. Retractions compose in the inclusion order and separate all analytic points. Enlargements add only trees to an old graph and subdivide its edges. Every type-II and type-III point belongs to some such graph; the complement of a core is a union of analytic open balls, with the usual disk classification and topology. For type-II vertices the graphs and refinements have value-group lengths. These are actual analytic and model assertions, not just a compact inverse-system declaration.

(R3) If $G$ is such a graph with value-group vertices and $f$ is rational-slope/value-group-valued PA with $\theta_G+\Delta f\geq0$, there is a refined **actual projective rational model on the same bundle** whose additive metric is $\psi_0+f\circ r_G$, whose special-component degrees are the atoms of $\theta_G+\Delta f$, and whose genuine continuous Monge--Ampere measure has those exact coefficients. Here $\theta_G$ has the old degrees and zero on contracted new components. The refined bundle is nef, and its metric is recognized and uniformly approximated by actual fixed-bundle FS metrics. Real PA positive-curvature limits then pass by the genuine continuous uniform law. Theorem 1 proves this last approximation step, but it does not prove the preceding model assertions.

(R4) On each complementary formal-fibre open ball, a local analytic frame of a cleared power of $L$ has constant $\psi_0$-norm. Adding a scalar factoring through $\Sigma_0$ retains that property. Nested finite disk ancestors converge to every terminal point, and analytic section norms obey disk inclusion there. This is the needed terminal-point geometry. It must be verified on actual charts; it is not granted by calling an abstract graph potential psh.

For original-field descent of the all-test criterion we further require (R5): for $X_C$ there is a nonempty finite $G_K$-orbit of actual type-II points. A model defined over a finite extension with geometrically split components would supply it, but the finite-extension existence assertion has not been checked recursively here. No fixed point of a Galois action on a graph with loops is assumed.

**Theorem 2 (conditional actual all-genus curve theorem).** Assuming (R1)--(R4) for the algebraically closed carrier, the genuine O operator solves every positive Radon target of raw mass $V$ and finite continuous dual. Every solution in the actual $\mathcal E^1$ cone differs by one finite real constant at every analytic point. The finite-dual condition equals integrability of every actual finite-energy potential, and the solution attains the variational supremum. If these hypotheses hold on the completed closure of an original nontrivial field, D transfers existence and every-solution uniqueness for finite-dual targets. With (R5), the downstairs all-$\mathcal E^1$ criterion also follows from a genuinely descended single norming atom. T handles trivial fields. This is an implication with unverified geometric antecedents, not an unconditional all-genus result.

Actual atom metrics under the geometric antecedents

Fix a type-II vertex $z$ of $\Sigma_0$. Theorem 1 solves and approximates the anchored real PA function $F_z$ with
$$
 F_z(z)=0,\qquad\theta+\Delta F_z=V\delta_z.
$$
Apply (R3) to each rational approximation. Its bundle is the actual old bundle tensored with the actual vertical rational Cartier divisor, rather than a numerical replacement. Its component degrees are nonnegative and its metric is actual continuous psh. Uniform limits and genuine continuous curvature continuity give the actual reference
$$
 \psi_z=\psi_0+F_z\circ r_{\Sigma_0},\qquad\operatorname{MA}(\psi_z)=V\delta_z.
$$
On a larger finite graph extend $F_z$ constantly along new trees. If $y$ is a type-II vertex, then
$$
 F_y=F_z-Vj_z(\cdot,y),\qquad\theta_G+\Delta F_y=V\delta_y.
$$
Theorem 1 and (R3) again give an actual continuous atom metric. Its scalar relative to $\psi_z$ is precisely
$$
 a_y=-Vj_z(\cdot,y),\qquad a_y(z)=0,\qquad\operatorname{MA}(a_y)=V\delta_y.
$$
For any type-III $y$ in an edge choose type-II points tending to it, using density of $\Lambda$. The kernel Lipschitz estimate makes the actual metrics converge uniformly, and $\delta_{y_i}\to\delta_y$ in the analytic topology. Thus the same assertion holds at type III. One does not apply Theorem 1 directly to a subdivision whose type-III edge lengths need not lie in $\Lambda$.

The global function $j_z(\cdot,y)$ is independent of the chosen finite graph containing $y$: the branch-extension formula leaves the kernel unchanged when one argument is in the old graph. Atom metrics are now actual operators' outputs. Before (R3) this notation is only graph data.

A genuine norming reference and weighted curve symmetry

Here and below scalars use $\psi_z$. For actual curve $p,q\in\mathcal E^1$, O's energy identity, affine law, and segment derivative imply
$$
 \int_Tp\,\operatorname{MA}(q)-\int_Tq\,\operatorname{MA}(p)
       =V\bigl(p(z)-q(z)\bigr). \tag{1}
$$
To verify the constant, expand $E((1-t)p+tq)=\frac12\int((1-t)p+tq)\operatorname{MA}((1-t)p+tq)+\frac V2((1-t)p(z)+tq(z))$ and compare its derivative at zero with O's $\int(q-p)\operatorname{MA}(p)$. Each integral is finite by O, and $p(z),q(z)$ are finite because O integrates each test against the reference output $V\delta_z$. No common pole values are subtracted.

For a continuous psh $p$ normalize $p(z)=0$, and use $q=a_y$. Equation (1) gives
$$
 p(y)=-\int_Tj_z(x,y)\,d\operatorname{MA}(p)(x)\leq0. \tag{2}
$$
Finite graph points are dense in $T$. A direct proof uses the real algebra generated by continuous functions pulled back from finite retractions: it separates points by (R2), and hence is uniformly dense in $C(T)$ by Stone--Weierstrass. Any fixed element is unchanged by every sufficiently large retraction. Therefore $r_Gx\to x$ against every continuous test, for each $x$. In particular the union of the finite graphs is dense. Continuity of $p$ proves $\sup_Tp=p(z)$.

Every FS scalar is continuous psh, so this establishes the exact N hypothesis for $\psi_z$, on the actual bundle. For an actual decreasing FS endpoint $p_i\downarrow p$, the finite numbers $p_i(z)=\sup p_i$ decrease. A limit of $-\infty$ would force $p\equiv-\infty$; otherwise the limit equals $p(z)=\sup p$. Thus all nontrivial actual psh endpoints are finite at the anchor. Only after this proof may N be applied. It gives the intrinsic all-test criterion over $C$.

Arbitrary support and a decreasing actual potential net

Let $\mu$ be any positive Radon measure on $T$ with mass $V$ and $J(\mu)<\infty$. Put $\nu=\mu/V$, $\mu_G=(r_G)_*\mu$, and
$$
 j_G(x,t)=j^G_z(r_Gx,r_Gt),\quad
 u_G(x)=-V\int_G j_z(r_Gx,y)\,d((r_G)_*\nu)(y).
$$
The kernel on $G^2$ is bounded and continuous. Its integral is uniformly approximated by finite convex averages of the **actual** $a_y$: partition the compact finite graph into Borel pieces of small metric diameter and use their actual probabilities. The Lipschitz bound controls the uniform error. Actual convexity and uniform closure give a continuous psh $u_G$. Curvature affinity on a curve and the genuine continuous uniform law give
$$
 \operatorname{MA}(u_G)=\mu_G,
$$
including diffuse edge measures. This is not the definition of an inverse measure construction: the genuine operator has already been constructed in O, and the displayed identity follows from its actual atom metrics and continuity.

The measures $\mu_G$ converge weakly to $\mu$. The same separating real algebra used above consists of finite combinations and products of pullbacks from finitely many graphs. One common larger graph fixes every such test under retraction. Uniform approximation and common mass $V$ give convergence against every original continuous function. No countable cofinal family or single skeleton replaces the original target support.

The branch-extension identity makes $j_G$ increase pointwise along the directed family, so $u_G$ decreases and $u_G(z)=0$. Define
$$
 I_G=\int_{T\times T}j_G(x,t)\,d\nu(x)d\nu(t).
$$
Only bounded continuous kernels and the ordinary product of two fixed Radon measures are used here. Fubini and the exact curve energy formula give
$$
 E(u_G)=-\frac{V^2}{2}I_G,\qquad
 \int_Tu_G\,d\mu=-V^2I_G,\qquad
 E(u_G)-\int_Tu_G\,d\mu=\frac{V^2}{2}I_G. \tag{3}
$$
In the first equality the reference integral $Vu_G(z)$ vanishes, and retracting both arguments does not change $j_G$. These are raw curve constants. When $V$ is not one, replacing $V^2$ by $V$ would be wrong.

Since the $u_G$ are actual continuous dual competitors, (3) bounds every energy cost by $J(\mu)$. Actual decreasing psh closure gives an all-point endpoint $u$ with $u(z)=0$, so it is not identically $-\infty$. O's **extended** decreasing-energy continuity gives
$$
 E(u)=\inf_GE(u_G)\geq-J(\mu)>-\infty.
$$
This establishes actual $\mathcal E^1$ membership before using any endpoint operator law. O then yields
$$
 \operatorname{MA}(u)=\lim_G\operatorname{MA}(u_G)=\lim_G\mu_G=\mu.
$$
There is no Hilbert-completion-to-actual-potential assertion and no arbitrary-net measurable monotone convergence.

Every solution and every terminal value

Let $p\in\mathcal E^1$ be any actual solution of this target, normalized by $p(z)=0$. The genuine weighted identity (1), tested with every actual atom $a_y$, yields
$$
 p(y)=-\int_Tj_z(x,y)\,d\mu(x)
$$
at every type-II and type-III point. All these values are finite, by O's integrability against the atom outputs. This determines every solution on the union of the finite graphs.

A terminal point $x$ lies in an open-ball branch of the fixed core. Use (R4) and the reference $\psi_z=\psi_0+F_z\circ r_{\Sigma_0}$. Its norm in a local cleared-power frame is constant on that ball. A section appearing in an FS system is analytic in this frame. On each closed disk strictly contained in the ball, an analytic section has a convergent power-series expansion and its Gauss norm is the supremum norm on the disk. Norms decrease under nested disk inclusion; the norm at the terminal seminorm is bounded by every ancestor norm. For type I the limiting disks have radius zero; for type IV they have empty intersection and positive limiting radius, as in Q's local disk classification. A ball isomorphism transfers this local classification, without importing any global genus-zero geometry.

Real FS weights add constants, finite weighted maxima retain disk monotonicity, and an actual decreasing FS net retains it at all points. Thus for finite ancestors $y_i\to x$ directed toward $x$,
$$
 p(x)\leq p(y_i),\qquad p(y_i)\downarrow\ell\geq p(x).
$$
Actual psh endpoints are upper semicontinuous, so $p(x)\geq\limsup_i p(y_i)=\ell$. Therefore $p(x)=\ell$, including a value of $-\infty$. This recovers every terminal value and proves all-point uniqueness. One never subtracts common negative infinities. The conclusion is $p=q+c$ at each point, in the extended-value sense.

Concavity and O's segment derivative at a solution give, for every actual $v\in\mathcal E^1$,
$$
 E(v)-E(u)\leq\int_T(v-u)\,d\mu.
$$
All integrals are legitimate on a common finite-value full-measure set. Hence the solution attains the variational supremum. Actual decreasing continuous majorants of $u$ converge in energy and in their integrals against the fixed output by O's weighted law. Thus the continuous dual equals the attained objective. Equation (3) and the same weighted law identify
$$
 J(\mu)=\frac{V^2}{2}\sup_GI_G,\qquad
 E(u)=-\frac{V^2}{2}\sup_GI_G,\qquad
 \int u\,d\mu=-V^2\sup_GI_G.
$$
Necessity of the intrinsic condition for outputs comes from O, and the norming reference already verified permits N to turn it into finite dual. C supplies genuine strict locality and comparison. The explicit decreasing construction and weighted uniqueness replace the use of normalized family compactness, envelope orthogonality, and both-sign outer differentiation in this conditional equation proof. No new theorem asserting those latter inputs in their full original domains is claimed.

Finite orbit, continuous averaging, and original-field descent

Now let $K$ be an original nontrivial field, $C=\widehat{\overline K}$, $Y=X_C^{\mathrm{an}}$, $G_K=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline K/K)$, and $\pi:Y\to X^{\mathrm{an}}$. Assume (R1)--(R4) upstairs and (R5). Take a nonempty finite orbit $S$ of type-II points. Start with any pulled-back invariant continuous psh reference $\psi_C$ on the actual $L_C$.

The conditional theorem just proved supplies a continuous actual atom metric $\phi_y$ of curvature $V\delta_y$ for every $y\in S$. Normalize each by $\sup_Y(\phi_y-\psi_C)=0$. Semilinear transport preserves actual FS systems, the continuous curvature operator, and its O decreasing limits. Every-solution all-point uniqueness upstairs therefore gives
$$
 g^*\phi_y=\phi_{g^{-1}y}
$$
with the appropriate pullback action convention; the supremum normalization kills its finite constant. In particular the finite continuous average
$$
 \phi_S=|S|^{-1}\sum_{y\in S}\phi_y
$$
is actual continuous psh and invariant. On the actual rational bundle this convex average is permitted by O; its coefficients are positive rational and its inputs are finite continuous metrics. Its genuine curvature is
$$
 \operatorname{MA}_C(\phi_S)=\frac{V}{|S|}\sum_{y\in S}\delta_y.
$$
D descends this continuous actual metric to $\psi_S$ downstairs. All orbit points have the same quotient image $\xi$. O's field pushforward gives $\operatorname{MA}_K(\psi_S)=V\delta_\xi$, with no degree multiplier.

The norming property requires an argument; invariance of an average alone is insufficient. Let $h$ be a continuous psh scalar against $\phi_S$, with positive genuine curvature $\alpha=\operatorname{MA}(\phi_S+h)$. Choose finite graphs containing the core, $z$, and $S$. The weighted identity against the $\psi_z$ atom metrics represents the restriction of $\phi_S+h-\psi_z$, up to its anchor constant, by the kernel potential of $\alpha_G=(r_G)_*\alpha$. The restriction of $\phi_S-\psi_z$ has curvature $\sigma=(V/|S|)\sum_S\delta_y$. Consequently $h|_G$ has graph curvature $\alpha_G-\sigma$. The finite-graph maximum-support lemma proves
$$
 \sup_G h=\max_S h.
$$
Density of the finite graphs and continuity give $\sup_Yh=\max_Sh$. If $h$ is the pullback of a downstairs scalar, its values on the single orbit $S$ agree. Thus every downstairs FS scalar satisfies $\sup h=h(\xi)$ against $\psi_S$. Decreasing FS endpoints extend this equality exactly as in N, excluding only the identically $-\infty$ endpoint. This verifies the **actual** N reference hypothesis downstairs, conditionally on the actual upstairs geometric antecedents and the finite orbit.

N can now establish that original-field all-$\mathcal E^1$ integrability is equivalent to finite $J_K$. For a target of finite $J_K$, D lifts it to its unique invariant Radon lift $\widetilde\mu$ of raw mass $V$, with $J_C(\widetilde\mu)=J_K(\mu)$. The actual upstairs construction applies to this target. Normalize its solution by supremum zero against the pulled-back invariant reference. Equivariance and **every-solution** uniqueness make it invariant. D descends the actual singular potential; D's extended energy equality applies before declaring its finite-energy membership. O's field pushforward then gives the original target equation.

For any other downstairs solution, O makes its pullback actual finite energy. Its upstairs curvature is invariant and pushes to the same target, so D's uniqueness of invariant lifts identifies it with $\widetilde\mu$. Upstairs uniqueness and surjectivity of $\pi$ give all-point equality modulo one finite constant downstairs. No noninvariant singular test is averaged or asserted to descend. Only the finite continuous atom average was used. Trivial fields are treated by T in its exact ample domain.

A potential alternative source of (R5) is a nonempty strictly affinoid domain defined over $K$: its upstairs finite Shilov boundary is Galois stable, and on a smooth curve its positive-dimensional boundary points are type II. A finite orbit would follow. This reduces the finite-extension issue but uses strict-affinoid boundary and reduction theorems not recursively checked here. It is recorded as a possible replacement, not a granted verification of (R5).

notes.text:
The actual geometric bridge: attempted proof and its remaining dependencies

The intended realization of Theorem 1 is concrete. Start with a pure FS metric on the actual bundle, not a numerical class. BE Theorem 5.14 gives its semiample projective rational model in its exact projective domain. One needs a strictly semistable dominating model, followed by refinements at value-group points. After clearing denominators, the graph approximants are integral $\Lambda$-affine. GH B.7 assigns an actual vertical Cartier divisor on the refined formal model. On a node chart $xy=\pi$, the equation is a value-group constant times an integral monomial; shared endpoint values make the ratios on overlaps units. Tensor the original model of $mL$ with this actual vertical divisor and divide by $m$.

The signs can be checked independently. For the canonical generic section $1$ of that vertical line bundle, the graph weight is $mG=-\log\|1\|$. Its generic divisor is zero. KRZB's formula reads $0=\operatorname{div}(mG)+\sum_v\deg(\mathcal O(D)|_{C_v})\delta_v$. Since their $\operatorname{div}$ is negative outgoing slope, the degree correction is $\Delta(mG)$. Therefore the tensor bundle has component degrees $m(\theta+\Delta G)$, positive at every graph vertex. On a reduced one-dimensional special fibre this is nef, indeed positive on each irreducible component. The single-point core is checked separately: its original degree is $V$, constants have zero correction, and nonconstant tests can be studied after adjoining a branch. KRZB's theorem explicitly excludes a one-point skeleton, so it cannot be invoked there unchanged.

For one inserted point of coordinate $t=\operatorname{val}(b)$ on a node of length $\operatorname{val}(\pi)$, the local admissible blowup has charts
$$
 xv=b,\quad y=(\pi/b)v;\qquad uy=\pi/b,\quad x=bu.
$$
Their subedge lengths are $t$ and $\operatorname{val}(\pi)-t$, both in the value group. These explicit charts verify the local subdivision and its flat equations. They do not by themselves verify global gluing, algebraization of the formal line bundle, projective recognition, or domination of every required old model over an arbitrary non-Noetherian valuation ring. A local chart computation is not the missing global theorem.

Once an actual nef projective rational model has been obtained, BE Theorem 7.8 recognizes its metric as psh for nontrivial fields and ample generic bundle. Its proof perturbs on an actual dominating projective model by an actual ample model of the same generic bundle and then uses Theorem 5.14. GM Proposition 4.11 and Lemma 4.12 are the supplied cited route to that ample domination. These results do not apply to an abstract graph distribution or a formal bundle that has not been put into their algebraic/projective domain.

The primary units checked in this turn expose the remaining recursive obligations. GH B.4 cites BL85 section 7 for semistable domination. GH B.6 cites GRW integral-unit slope results; B.7 uses analytic-unit/model-divisor identification, and B.8 uses the strictly semistable subdivision construction. BPR's complete 4.15 proof uses BL85 formal fibres, the canonical-model facts, and formal/algebraic recognition; its 4.2(2) points to Abbes for non-Noetherian algebraization. KRZB Theorem 2.6 uses an analytic meromorphic slope extension, with a precise footnote pointing to CTT, not only the algebraic BPR statement. GJKM section 3 contains an explicit non-Noetherian algebraization claim via Abbes/Fujiwara--Kato and a finite-extension semistable domination claim via BL85. None of these recursive units was certified by working observation228, and some have not been obtained here.

Direct standard-library downloads of all seven designated PDFs failed immediately with `PermissionError(1, Operation not permitted)`. The allowed web tool did retrieve the literal GH v2, BPR v1, KRZB v3, BE v3, GM2019, and GJKM v3 documents. It could not retrieve the specified BL85 PDF, two public alternate download paths, or the full Springer article; the latter yielded only a subscription preview. A fresh public search found the EuDML record at <https://eudml.org/doc/182964>, but opening it failed with a timeout; the gdz volume viewer was also inaccessible through the tool. The Abbes author page yielded bibliography and descriptions, not the required full algebraization proof. No account, installation, network-setting, proxy, CA, runtime, or sandbox change was attempted. These failures are evidence of this turn's unverified source boundary, not a statement that the established source theorems are false.

Accordingly (R1)--(R5) are not removed from Theorem 2. The finite graph theorem is proved, but its application to every actual original curve is not established by this submission under the requested recursive proof rule. We do not use the public genus-zero paper as an extra grant, do not claim a new unconditional theorem by repeating Q, and do not promote working observation228 to a seventh grant.

It checks 140 specified interpolation cases on four graphs (parallel irrational cycles, signed starting curvature, unequal weights, and a subdivided self-loop), kernel symmetry and tree-extension identities, the singleton case, and 210 raw-mass/energy cases on a fixed branched cyclic graph. python3 graph_checks.py

